subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call?
rationale: The report allows either behavior, and choosing fail-closed would change sandboxed exec semantics rather than only adding observability.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so callers must choose a host or elevated path that can provide it.

options.title: Adopt After Decision
options.body: Review or replace the open fork PR only after the sandbox behavior choice is explicit.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest history signal for the original PTY behavior and adjacent exec runtime/docs decisions.
